solutionIdeas.headline: GLP-1 muscle loss and nausea risk comparison by peptide stack

They then browse a curated list of common muscle-preserving adjunct peptides—Tesamorelin, CJC-1295, Ipamorelin, BPC-157, MK-677—and click to generate a protocol comparison page. Each page displays aggregated FAERS adverse-event counts: nausea incidence per 1,000 reports for the GLP-1 alone versus the GLP-1 + peptide combination, plus muscle-loss/muscle-wasting report rates. Risk ratios are color-coded (green/yellow/red) for instant scanning. Users can filter by risk tolerance, view raw FAERS case counts, and export a summary PDF for their provider. The site updates quarterly when FDA releases new FAERS batches, ensuring risk estimates stay current as prescribing patterns evolve.

Each trial card displays a "Dosing Map" showing mg/kg schedules, administration frequency, and trial phase, plus a "Relevance Score" based on how closely the trial matches the user's selected condition profile. Users can drill into any trial to see the original protocol alongside the translated summary, track trial status updates (recruiting, active, completed), and view published results when available. Behind the scenes, the system continuously monitors ClinicalTrials.gov API and PubMed via daily polling, detecting new TA1 trial registrations and result publications. When new trials appear or status changes occur, users receive instant email alerts with summary highlights and direct links to the updated trial pages. The platform also maintains a historical archive of all TA1 trials ever registered, enabling users to track research trends over time and compare dosing approaches across different conditions.

solutionIdeas.name: Peptide TrialLens + Safety Math Kit

tags.rationale: regulatory: clinical trial/health data; subscription: freemium with recurring Pro tier; continuous: ongoing dosing/storage tracking.

solutionIdeas.headline: Clinical trial briefs and dosing calculators for peptide research
solutionIdeas.description: Users arrive and search for a specific peptide (e.g., BPC-157, Thymosin Alpha-1) or condition (e.g., Long COVID, tendon repair). The product returns a structured brief summarizing relevant clinical trials with eligibility criteria translated into plain English, highlighting studied populations and evidence quality. Users then access deterministic calculators to convert reconstitution math—entering peptide mass, bacteriostatic water volume, and desired dose—to draw volumes in milliliters or units. A storage scheduler prompts for reconstitution date and peptide type, then generates a calendar-based potency timeline with refrigeration reminders. Throughout, a rules layer flags high-risk contexts: cancer history triggers angiogenesis warnings for BPC-157/TB-500, and mood effect alerts appear for compounds with reported anhedonia/depression signals. Users can export a clinician-ready packet summarizing trial evidence, dosing calculations, and safety flags to discuss with healthcare providers.
